sourceOccurrences.label: Universal off-critical capped mean
sourceOccurrences.relationship: Proof with stated scope and remaining inputs
sourceOccurrences.note: Includes real caps, infinite susceptibility and the continuity/range justification for the intermediate value argument.

proofUses.reason: Includes real caps, infinite susceptibility and the continuity/range justification for the intermediate value argument.

Analytic moments and threshold divergence justify the moment-ratio scale. Truncation, tree-graph second moments and endpoint domination give the integrated bound; finite-set sharpness identifies the threshold.
A scale enlarged by the square of the upper logarithmic factor separates the initial mass from the monotone tail; the ceiling and initial range are retained.
An intermediate-value choice of t, the truncated mean bound (LLGA) with lambda=2 and stochastic domination give the claim; the integer form uses the tail-sum identity (CSY8).

The row-sum bound (JZ47), finite-set sharpness (L0TE) and right-openness with endpoint divergence (5LNL) give a continuous unbounded susceptibility; the tree-graph bound (Y84V) supplies cubic moments for the interpolation theorem F75G.
MXGM gives continuity and the susceptibility lower bound, Y84V and F75G the integrated tail; QS3L and the pointwise upgrade MBV2 give the tail from the susceptibility, and 1EJP the converse.

UPMK links the first two conditions; LZCK and the tree-graph bound (Y84V) give the fourth from the first; Z9K8 with the universal derivative bounds of MXGM give the third; integration returns the first.
